text.title: user-flows.md Template Core Rules
text.summary: 7 testable rules every per-feature user-flows.md MUST satisfy: when it is required and when it is forbidden, the five fields per flow, the 1:1 Playwright mapping, and the pos+neg rule with its unsexy-edge corollary. HARD rules — user-supplied input cannot override them.

rule.statement: If the feature has any user-facing flow (page navigation, form submission, button click, command invocation), user-flows.md MUST exist before the feature can be promoted to done/.
rule.rationale: A user-facing flow without a documented happy / negative path is a flow nobody is actually testing. The artefact is the only forcing function.

rule.statement: Backend-only features (no rendered surface) MUST NOT have user-flows.md. They verify through API tests in `tests/api/`.
rule.rationale: The artefact tracks behaviour the user can observe. Pure backend work is verified through API tests, not user-flow specs. Forcing user-flows.md on backend work produces empty templates and conditions reviewers to skim past the artefact when it matters.

rule.statement: Every flow MUST list all five fields — Actor, Preconditions, Happy path, Negative paths, Playwright spec path. Missing fields fail the readiness gate.
rule.rationale: Each flow in user-flows.md has five required fields. The fields jointly describe the contract between feature and test suite. Dropping any one breaks the 1:1 mapping.

rule.statement: The Happy path is numbered steps with an expected result per step; the success criterion is in the final step.
rule.rationale: A step without an expected result cannot be asserted; a success criterion buried mid-flow leaves the spec's final assertion undefined.

rule.statement: Each negative path states its trigger (what causes the error) and the expected error UX (what the user sees, where).
rule.rationale: Trigger plus expected UX is what a Playwright negative case asserts; without both the negative cannot be automated.

rule.statement: Each flow MUST document at least one happy-path case AND at least one negative-path case.
rule.rationale: Every flow MUST carry at least one positive AND one negative case. Positive-only coverage is a smoke test: it proves the path works under perfect conditions. Production bugs hide on imperfect paths. The negative case is what catches actual production bugs.

rule.statement: Every flow names the relative path to the Playwright spec file that automates it; flows map 1:1 to spec files.
rule.rationale: The five fields together map 1:1 to a Playwright spec file; reviewers use the spec to navigate the suite, and the mapping is what lets a pipeline verify pos+neg coverage before close-out.

section.title: Conclusion targets used by the decision tree

rule.statement: Run the full procedure; emit user-flows.md passing the output contract with every flow linked to its spec.
rule.rationale: Terminal target used by 06-decision-tree when the feature has a user-facing flow and the artefact passes every shape check.

rule.statement: Skip; the feature is outside the SDD feature lifecycle or the project has no Playwright (or equivalent) E2E harness.
rule.rationale: Terminal target used by 06-decision-tree when preconditions fail.
